subject: Aurum Health - multi-region bundled SKU ask and channel uplift coordination
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal ask — multi-region bundle + reseller uplift for Aurum

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Aurum’s procurement team asked for a single private offer that covers: reserved capacity in us-east and eu-central, plus metered burst credits across both regions, bundled under a single SKU family. They also want a channel uplift passed to their EU reseller (GlobalMed Solutions) so the reseller can keep their margin intact when reselling locally.

Can you confirm the following so we can price correctly:
- Expected committed node-hours (year 1) per region (rough numbers are fine)
- Whether Aurum requires invoice routing to GlobalMed for EU purchases or prefers Redwood invoicing and reseller settlement
- Any VAT/withholding handling they require on our invoice

I attached a draft pricing workbook (aurum_pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx) and an SOW stub for reference. If the procurement team can provide commitment bands (e.g., 50k node-hours, 150k, 300k) we’ll put together a tiered discount and a suggested channel uplift to preserve reseller economics.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min sync tomorrow to align on exact commitment bands and passback mechanics.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0121

Attachments: aurum_pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Aurum_MultiRegion_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub)

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@aurumhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurumhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposal ask — multi-region bundle + reseller uplift for Aurum

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary.

Quick answers:
- We can start with rough commitments: EU 120k node-hours / year, US 80k node-hours. Will confirm numbers after internal finance readout on Wed.
- Aurum prefers Redwood invoice for consolidated billing but needs evidence that GlobalMed will receive a pass-through margin; they don’t want separate invoices routed by default.
- VAT should be applied per local rules; Aurum needs us to support net-of-VAT pricing on the PO (their finance team will issue guidance).

I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@aurumhealth.com) who can send a formal commitment matrix. Happy to do the 30-min sync Wednesday 08:30 PT.

Best,
Sam

Subject: Fwd: Aurum commitments — pricing / channel uplift discussion (internal)

Folks — forwarding Aurum’s reply and procurement loop-in. High level asks that affect pricing and channel math:
1) They want consolidated Redwood invoicing but expect GlobalMed to receive a pass-through uplift (so reseller keeps margin).
2) Commitments: EU 120k / US 80k (pending confirmation).
3) VAT handling: net-of-VAT phrasing on PO, but they want to understand how reseller uplift impacts tax/treatment.

Open questions for ops/legal/finance:
- Do we structure the private offer prices gross (list) with explicit channel uplift as a separate line item that gets netted to GlobalMed? Or do we embed resale margin into list price and settle with GlobalMed off-invoice?
- If we do on-invoice uplift, what evidence does procurement need to accept our approach (signed reseller agreement + proof of reseller VAT registration?)

I sketched a quick starting point in channel_margin_calc.xlsx (attached) — proposing a 10–12% uplift on EU list for GlobalMed to preserve their margin after VAT and marketplace fees. Low-level example included.

Goal: keep Aurum’s unit economics predictable while not breaking GlobalMed’s commercial model. Can Ben/ Priya weigh in on the margin and ops implications?

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachments: channel_margin_calc.xlsx (model)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurum commitments — pricing / channel uplift discussion (internal)

Vanessa — good notes. A few practical points from pricing/ops perspective:
- Prefer explicit uplift as a separate line on the private offer where possible. That keeps list price clean for internal reporting and makes it easier to show Aurum how their effective unit price changes with/without the reseller pass-through.
- For EU, a 12% uplift sounds defensible given: local VAT (~20–25% depending country), marketplace fees (~3–5%), and reseller margin target (8–12%). We should model country-level VAT, not a single EU average — Aurum operates across DE/FR/IE so that matters.
- If we do on-invoice uplift, procurement will want: signed reseller agreement + reseller VAT registration number + a short pass-through statement on the SOW. Finance needs to confirm whether we should treat the uplift as a contra-revenue or as a reseller payout (affects revenue recognition). I’ll flag to accounting.

I attached a quick worksheet with country-level cells and sample arithmetic. I recommend we:
1) Build a tiered private offer (3 bands) with explicit uplift per band;
2) Draft an SOW paragraph describing pass-through mechanics and evidence required;
3) Ask procurement if they can confirm invoice preference (consolidated to Aurum vs routed).

Ben
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: channel_margin_calc.xlsx (updated with country cells)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurum commitments — pricing / channel uplift discussion (internal)

Adding procurement ops notes:
- Evidence checklist for on-invoice pass-through (attached): signed reseller agreement, GlobalMed VAT registration, proof of reseller onboarding in marketplace (if reseller wants to list), and confirmation of settlement cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
- For marketplace listings where reseller is an intermediary, our recommmendation is consolidated invoicing to customer + a monthly settlement report to reseller with exact uplift amounts — that minimizes tax fragmentation.
- We should also document how credits/true-ups are handled if usage is metered and crosses bands mid-month. Recommend language in SOW: Redwood will calculate uplift on actual billed usage and remit to reseller within 30 days, subject to reconciliation.

I attached evidence_checklist.pdf and a short template SOW paragraph. Once Aurum confirms bands we can finalize pricing and put the DocuSign amendment in motion.

Priya
Senior Deal Ops | Redwood Inference
